label: S2-good belief signal (high when S2 believed good), D1 dominated by last reward
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * ((prev_reward == 1) == (prev_state == 2)) * (prev_state > 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (belief - 0.5) ;; (phase == D2) * (belief - 0.5)
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 19 encodes an a2 / S2-good signal from observed history. At GO and D2 it falls steeply with the ideal-observer belief that S1 is good (weights about -0.9 at GO and -1.2 at D2 on belief-0.5): high when S2 is believed good, low when S1 is. At D2 it is also higher when S2 is the reached state (+0.43) and lower after an unrewarded previous trial (-0.27). At GO it is a little higher after a previous a2 choice (+0.15). At D1 the main driver is the reward just shown: about -0.9 after an unrewarded trial. On top of that it is higher after a previous a2 choice (+0.45) and slightly higher after S2-favouring outcomes (S2 rewarded or S1 unrewarded, +0.13). D1 belief adds almost nothing. No future, hidden or model-output variables are used. Dev R^2 beyond timing is 0.78 against an all-observed ceiling of 0.89 and an all-cue ceiling of 0.93. Belief alone (decile table) reaches 0.52 and the model policy decile reaches 0.61, so the observed-only belief plus trial-history terms lose essentially nothing relative to the model-policy explanation. Remaining misses: D1 after a2 S1 u and a1 S1 r is under-predicted, and D1 after a1 S2 u is over-predicted.

issues: The headline score reproduces: the 8 terms give test R^2 beyond timing 0.773, with weights matching the explanation (D1 prev_reward==0 -0.89, D1 prev a2 +0.45, D1 S2-favouring +0.13, GO prev a2 +0.15, D2 state S2 +0.43, D2 prev_reward==0 -0.27, GO belief -0.89, D2 belief -1.22). The GO/D2 belief claim holds: in the profile the residual falls monotonically by belief decile, from +0.47 to -0.57 at GO and +0.65 to -0.70 at D2.

The D1 claim 'slightly higher after outcomes that favour S2 (S2 rewarded or S1 unrewarded)' is half wrong. The D1 residual by previous trial is a1 S1 r +0.25 vs a1 S2 r +0.07, and a2 S1 r +0.51 vs a2 S2 r +0.48. So S2-rewarded is NOT higher than S1-rewarded. The +0.13 comes only from the unrewarded side (a1 S1 u -0.95 vs a1 S2 u -1.21; a2 S1 u +0.01 vs a2 S2 u -0.64).

D1 has a real interaction that the additive terms miss: after a2 S1 u the residual is about 0 (+0.01), while after the other unrewarded patterns it is -0.6 to -1.2. In the original fit's misses, D1 after a2 S1 u is under-predicted by +0.35, D1 after a1 S1 r by +0.28 and D1 after a1 S2 u is over-predicted by -0.29, giving a D1 mean error of +0.10. A full D1 last-trial table removes most of this (D1 cell errors drop to about 0.15) and raises test R^2 to 0.795.

'Belief at D1 adds almost nothing' overclaims. Swapping the S2-favouring term for (phase==D1)*(belief-0.5) scores the same (0.772 vs 0.773; weight -0.14). The profile's D1 residual by belief decile spans +0.39 to -0.36. Belief and the S2-favouring term are interchangeable at D1, so neither is uniquely the driver.

The phrase 'loses essentially nothing compared with the earlier model-policy explanation' is not backed by the numbers given. 0.61 is the score of the policy-decile table alone, not of the earlier explanation, so the size of the loss is not established. The observed-only additive ceiling is 0.89, so a gap of about 0.1 to 0.12 remains.

Remaining errors after better terms: D2 by previous trial is still off by about 0.2 (under-predicted after a2 S2 u by +0.21, over-predicted after a1 S1 u by -0.22). D2 mean error is -0.08 to -0.09 and D1 mean error is +0.09 with every term set tried. Neither D2 prev_action nor D2 action terms fixed this (test 0.778 to 0.797).
